summary: Linear search checks items one at a time. Binary search halves a sorted array on each step, so it needs far fewer comparisons on long arrays.
notes: (low + high) / 2 is int division in Java, so mid is already a whole number.
low = mid + 1 and high = mid - 1 skip mid, because it was already checked.
A Java method returns one value, so each search returns an int[] holding the index and the count.
pitfall: Running binary search on an unsorted array gives wrong answers with no error, often -1 for a value that is in the array.
